name: WordPress
support: Open-source software; maintained by the WordPress open-source project and supported by a large hosting and developer ecosystem.
technology: Server: PHP </br> Database: MySQL or MariaDB </br> Client: HTML, CSS and JavaScript; themes control presentation and plugins extend functionality.
capabilities: Themes and plugins; visual/block editing; custom post types; REST API; large ecosystem for commerce, SEO, forms and multilingual sites.
limitations: Site owners must manage hosting and updates for self-hosted installs. Third-party plugins/themes can introduce compatibility, performance and security risks; advanced customization may require PHP knowledge.

name: Drupal
support: Open-source software supported by the Drupal community and commercial service providers.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL or SQLite (version-dependent). Client: HTML, CSS and JavaScript; commonly extended with Composer-managed modules.
capabilities: Flexible content types and fields; roles and permissions; taxonomy; multilingual publishing; contributed modules; APIs and structured content for complex sites.
limitations: More complex to build and administer than simpler site builders. Module compatibility, upgrades and configuration can require specialist development and ongoing maintenance.

name: Joomla
support: Open-source CMS maintained by the Joomla project and supported by its community and service providers.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL (supported versions vary). Client: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with templates and extensions.
capabilities: Template-based design; extensions; multilingual features; user groups and access control; custom fields; menu management and built-in content workflows.
limitations: Smaller extension and theme ecosystem than WordPress. Major-version upgrades and third-party extensions can require compatibility checks and technical administration.

name: Wix CMS
support: Commercial, hosted website-building platform provided by Wix; core platform is proprietary.
technology: Managed cloud platform. Browser-based visual editor and CMS collections; front-end components can be connected to structured content. Wix does not publish a complete underlying server/database stack.
capabilities: Visual site builder; CMS collections and dynamic pages; connected repeaters and forms; hosting and platform maintenance handled by Wix; built-in SEO and app integrations.
limitations: Less server-level control than self-hosted systems; portability and migration can be limited; advanced custom behavior is constrained by the platform's supported APIs and editor model.

name: Shopify
support: Commercial hosted e-commerce platform operated by Shopify; subscription-based service with an app and partner ecosystem.
technology: Hosted SaaS platform. Themes commonly use Liquid templates, HTML, CSS and JavaScript; store data is managed by Shopify. Storefront and Admin APIs support integrations.
capabilities: Product catalog and inventory; checkout and payments integrations; themes; apps; sales channels; order management; storefront customization and APIs.
limitations: Optimized primarily for commerce rather than general-purpose publishing. Subscription and app costs can add up; platform rules and checkout/database access limit low-level control.

name: Ghost
support: Open-source publishing platform; users can self-host or purchase managed hosting through Ghost(Pro).
technology: Server: Node.js. Database: MySQL in supported production deployments. Client: HTML, CSS and JavaScript; themes use Handlebars templates and content is accessible through APIs.
capabilities: Publishing and memberships; newsletters; paid subscriptions; editorial workflows; themes; integrations and Content API/Admin API.
limitations: Focused on publishing, newsletters and memberships rather than broad enterprise content modeling. Self-hosting requires server administration; some integrations or advanced features may need external services.

name: Contentful
support: Commercial cloud-based headless content platform operated by Contentful, with plans and developer tooling for teams.
technology: API-first hosted service with structured content delivered through HTTP APIs, including JSON responses. Front-end can be built with JavaScript or other languages; the customer chooses the presentation stack.
capabilities: Structured reusable content models; headless delivery across websites and apps; APIs and SDKs; localization; roles/workflows and integrations with modern front-end frameworks.
limitations: Does not provide a complete traditional website theme/editor experience by itself; a separate front-end is usually required. Cost and complexity can grow with usage, content modeling and integrations.

name: Umbraco
support: Open-source .NET CMS with commercial cloud hosting and support options from Umbraco and its partner ecosystem.
technology: Server: .NET/C#. Database: SQL Server or SQLite depending on setup. Client: HTML, CSS and JavaScript; Razor views and APIs support custom presentation.
capabilities: Flexible content types; customizable back office; templates and extensions; multilingual content; APIs and integrations within the .NET ecosystem.
limitations: Best suited to teams comfortable with .NET and its hosting ecosystem. More advanced implementations can require developer expertise; package compatibility should be checked during upgrades.
